top_story.headline: CACI gets a $152.8 million sole-source ceiling increase on an Army support task order
top_story.dek: The General Services Administration says internal funding realignments are exhausted and only a ceiling increase can sustain operations.
paragraphs: The General Services Administration, acting for the Army's C5ISR Center, posted a justification for an exception to fair opportunity that raises the ceiling on the Global Operational Support, Information Insight, and Threat task order held by CACI by $152,779,419. The task order was competitively awarded on May 20, 2024 with a ceiling of $414,857,176 and runs through May 2029.
The justification says earlier funding realignments are completely exhausted and an immediate ceiling increase is the only viable way to sustain operations.

Elsewhere in today's postings, two bridge contracts trace to protests: the Army Corps of Engineers wants a bridge for fuel-system maintenance, and the Navy wants a third bridge for Naval District Washington custodial services after two Government Accountability Office protests.

sections.headline: CACI gets a $152.8 million sole-source ceiling increase; protests drive two bridge contracts
paragraphs: 52 new sole-source justifications and 921 new solicitations; 0 notices already covered in earlier editions are not repeated. The five items below are the ones with the clearest news value; the rest are listed by agency.

blocks.title: Army Corps of Engineers seeks sole-source bridge for fuel-system maintenance at 45 installations while a protest of the follow-on award is pending
meta: Vendor not named in the posted document
Value redacted
Urgent need, no time to compete
Department of Defense (U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, for the Defense Logistics Agency)
blocks.text: The Army Corps of Engineers Huntsville center wants a bridge contract of up to 336 days (a 66-day base plus three 90-day options) for preventive and emergency repair of the Air Force fuels program, starting September 29, 2026, right after the current task order expires on September 28. The justification says the bridge is needed to avoid a gap in service while protest litigation over the successor contract remains active; it adds that the incumbent already has the workforce, installation access and maintenance records to continue without a transition period.

blocks.title: Navy asks for a third bridge for Washington-area custodial services after two Government Accountability Office protests
meta: NJS Joint Venture, LLC
Value redacted
Urgent need, no time to compete
Department of Defense (Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Washington)
blocks.text: The Navy wants a 12-month bridge (a two-month base plus ten one-month options, October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027) for custodial services at Naval District Washington facilities. The justification says a pre-award protest filed March 16, 2026 delayed proposal evaluations, and that after the Government Accountability Office dismissed it, a second protest was received May 22, 2026.

blocks.title: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services sole-sources follow-on support for court-ordered family reunification of separated families
meta: International Organization for Migration
Value redacted
Urgent need, no time to compete
Department of Homeland Security
blocks.text: The follow-on covers help with parole and work-authorization applications, travel booking, pre-departure briefings and a help desk for families covered by the Miss L. v. Immigration and Customs Enforcement settlement. The incumbent contract, first awarded to the International Organization for Migration on August 13, 2021, ran through September 12, 2026 on option periods; the document says responsibility moved from Immigration and Customs Enforcement to the agency in late fiscal 2025, and that a lapse would violate the settlement.

blocks.title: Immigration and Customs Enforcement sole-sources 366 parking spaces near its D.C. headquarters, citing protests and the return-to-office order
meta: Potomac Center CF, LLC
Value redacted
Only one company can do it
Department of Homeland Security (U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement)
blocks.text: The agency would buy 366 underground spaces at the Potomac Center South garage in Washington, D.C. for government vehicles. The justification says the spaces are needed for overflow capacity because of a surge in accommodation requests and parking demand under the Executive Order on Return to In-Person Work, and says the garage provides emergency access and egress for employees during protests or building lockdowns.

sections.headline: No new awards of $2 million or more; four mid-size awards stand out
paragraphs: No new contract awards of $2 million or more appeared in the September 14 to October 9 sweep. Among 45 new awards between $100,000 and $2 million, four were flagged.

items: Deloitte Consulting LLP — $1,199,958.75, National Aeronautics and Space Administration: program support for systems engineering, integration and risk management on the lunar landing missions at Marshall Space Flight Center (award).
Fasone Construction, Inc. — $1,147,809.73, General Services Administration: task order for hardening (security upgrades) at the Richard H. Chambers Courthouse in Pasadena, California (award).
Procare Ambulance of Maryland, Inc. — $1,252,145.65, Department of Veterans Affairs: first ordering period of ambulance services for the Washington, D.C. medical center (award).

Hirt Electric, LLC — $585,400, Department of Veterans Affairs: replacing chillers in Building 1W at the Huntington, West Virginia medical center; the description notes a new contract clause on diversity, equity and inclusion discrimination (award).

blocks.text: 45 new awards under $2 million were screened; all 4 flagged awards are listed above and 41 routine ones are not, led by the Department of Veterans Affairs (22) and the General Services Administration (5). One award worth $1.2 million cites Executive Order 14398 in its description.

sections.headline: No new apportionments approved this week
paragraphs: No new apportionment files were released by the Office of Management and Budget during the October 4–9 window. Spend Plan updates were checked across 145 federal agencies, with no new or revised plans published.
